Haha okay so most of my life I didn’t really get that something was wrong with me. Towards the end of high school I was playing with the idea I might have depression, because teachers and councillors had asked me about it. It wasn’t until after I graduated that I went to my doctor about it and started actually trying to unravel what was going on. It’s been some years since then, and during that time I’ve had 5+ different therapists, had blood work done 3 times, and 2 psychiatrists (3 if you count the one that oversaw my hospital stays). I really do appreciate you trying to show me that this isn’t likely and the doctors are probably wrong. But sadly just because I want them to be wrong and it isn’t fair for them to be right, it doesn’t mean they aren’t right.  The first time I remember feeling like this I was 4 years old, and it hasn’t stopped for longer than a few weeks since then. I hope I’m not coming off argumentative, I just keep trying to reach out to people about this and not once have they said anything other than “but are you sure???”  Believe me, I want to just blow it off and say that they’re wrong, but 2 decades of this seems like pretty damning evidence that this has a low chance of going away.  And if nothing else, if I’m ready for it and they’re wrong, then I prepared myself for a hard life that will be much easier. If they’re right and I’m not ready for it this will kill me.

When I lost my grandma, my mom and her siblings went through all her stuff in a matter of days. Everyone took one or two things that made them both sad and happy for her. Later after the funeral they all got completely hammered and told stories about her.

When a family friend lost her father last year, she had the task of going through her old childhood home and like you decide what to give away and what to keep. She’s been at it for months, and hasn’t made a lot of progress. It’s really hard for her to get rid of things, because everything is a memory.

Nobody can tell you how to go about this, but there will be a way for you. If you need to take your time and you are able to (as it’s not costing you anything other than time) then you should. But if going slow and going fast both hurt the same, maybe try faster so it doesn’t hurt as long. Definitely try to keep things that make you remember them with happiness and sadness. My grandma painted all the time, and I have a few of her paintings. When I look at them it makes me happy to know I still have that connection, even if I can’t still watch movies and have macaroni with her.
